inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 460.98M basic on the Q2-2026 10-Q cover (dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding, 2026-06-30) plus ~2.0M dilutive awards (Q2-2026 diluted 464.52M less basic 462.53M weighted average). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; the $4.6B/yr buyback is the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat and is already charged as SBC.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement share-based compensation add-back ($164M; Metrics.csv StockBasedComp). XBRL carries no PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation tag and the filer publishes no combined equity-award figure, so no withholding tax is added; at 0.5% of revenue the omission is immaterial.
inputs.debt_source: Q2-2026 10-Q, XBRL DebtLongtermAndShorttermCombinedAmount $28,013M = short-term borrowings $4,861M + long-term debt incl. current portion $23,152M. NOTE: Metrics.csv TotalDebt 25,626 is LongTermDebt + LongTermDebtCurrent, which double-counts the $2,474M current portion and omits the $4,861M of short-term borrowings; the same construction holds on FY2025 (CSV 24,275 vs filer 26,989). Not used here.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD-built WACC. Risk-free ~4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.85-0.9 -> cost of equity ~8.5-8.7%; after-tax cost of debt ~3.7% (A/A2 rated, ~4.9% pre-tax); net debt ~10% of enterprise value -> WACC ~8.0%. Held identical across all three scenarios: cyclicality, backlog execution and policy risk are charged in the flows, not stacked into the rate (adaptations 7f).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), as already embedded in US GAAP: ASC 842 operating lease cost ($250M/yr payments, $866M liability at FY2025) is a straight-line operating expense inside EBIT and inside the EBITDA margin path, so lease liabilities are excluded from total_debt. Finance leases ($214M liability) sit inside the filer's long-term debt figure and are therefore in net debt; their principal is not separately deducted from the flows. One treatment, applied once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are modelled on the consolidated basis (EBITDA includes the ~2.3% of profit attributable to non-controlling interests, $160M in FY2025; NCI equity $1,536M at 2026-06-30). NCI is charged ONCE, in the equity bridge, at $2,900M = FY2025 NCI share of net income $160M x ~18x, which is consistent with the equity/attributable-NI multiple the base case itself implies (~17-18x) rather than the $1.5B book value. Not also folded into the tax/leakage rate.
inputs.equity_investees: Equity-method investments ($2,015M book at FY2025; $150M income in FY2025) are below operating income, so their income is outside the EBITDA-built flows. Matching-asset rule: the asset is added back in the bridge at book value (conservative versus ~$2.7B at an earnings multiple).
inputs.pension: Net defined-benefit liability $473M (FY2025 10-K, non-current) treated as debt-like and deducted in the bridge; service cost is already inside EBIT.
inputs.timing_note: valuation_date is 2026-10-02 but FY0 = FY2025 and Year 1 = FY2026 is discounted a full period, although nine months of FY2026 have elapsed; this understates value by roughly three quarters of a year of discounting (~5-6%) and is deliberately left conservative. Net debt and the share count are the latest (2026-06-30) and therefore already reflect H1-2026 free cash flow ($1,731M) and H1-2026 distributions ($1,479M dividends + $1,678M buybacks).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (owner-fcf.md + adaptations 7b/7c/7d for leases, NCI and equity investees), 10-year explicit horizon because capex is in a backlog supercycle (15.5% of revenue in FY2025, guided $5.5-6.0B for FY2026 vs ~10% of revenue in FY2021-22) and the owner-FCF margin is still ramping at year 5 as that spend normalises. Linde is a US GAAP, USD filer quoted in USD on NYSE/Nasdaq. EBITDA margin paths are stated BEFORE SBC (GAAP EBITDA 12,686 + SBC 164 = 12,850 = 37.8% of FY2025 revenue; H1-2026 38.6%) because the engine subtracts sbc_pct_path from them. FY2025 EBITDA carried $273M of restructuring charges (0.8pp); H1-2026 carried none. Cash tax 25.5% of engine EBIT ties exactly to FY2025 income taxes paid ($2,274M on EBIT $8,923M); the GAAP ETR is 22% but non-deductible Linde AG purchase-accounting amortisation (~$0.8B/yr, rolling off over the horizon) sits in D&A, so the engine's EBIT-based rate is set higher and drifts down as that amortisation unwinds. Working capital: receivables + inventory exceed payables + contract liabilities, so growth consumes cash (wc_capture -5% of the revenue increase). Interest income ($209M FY2025) is not deducted because the company is a large net borrower (net interest expense $255M); the EBITDA-built flows exclude it anyway. Buyback_cash is actual FY2025 financing outflow ($4,601M), so the flat count is genuinely funded. Reported FCF calibration: engine-style FY2025 owner FCF = NOPAT 6,648 + D&A 3,763 - capex 5,261 - WC ~49 = ~5,100 vs reported FCF 5,089 less SBC 164 plus after-tax net interest ~250 = ~5,175 unlevered; within 2%.

equity_bridge.item: Equity-method investments at book (income excluded from flows)
equity_bridge.note: FY2025 10-K, EquityMethodInvestments; $150M FY2025 equity income sits below operating income

equity_bridge.item: Non-controlling interests at ~18x FY2025 NCI profit share
equity_bridge.note: NCI share of net income $160M FY2025; book NCI $1,536M at 2026-06-30 would understate the claim

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Forward underlying run-rate: ~2% price + ~2% volume (Q2-2026 underlying +4%) plus backlog start-ups ($8.1B sale-of-gas backlog, >20 start-ups in H2-2026), tapering to 3% terminal. None of the historical CAGRs is a usable anchor: equity shrinks because $4-5B/yr of buybacks exceed retained earnings; FY2022 revenue was inflated ~$3B by energy cost pass-through that unwound in FY2023 (3yr revenue CAGR 0.6% is a pass-through artefact, not a volume story); EPS CAGRs (21-25%) are flattered by the 2019-20 merger-integration trough base and the buyback.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-1.3% 3yr / -4.3% 5yr) diverges by far more than 30% from revenue (0.6% / 4.5%) and EPS (21.0% / 25.3%). Cause: capital return exceeding earnings (FY2025 dividends $2.8B + buybacks $4.6B vs net income $7.1B) and Linde AG merger goodwill/intangibles amortising out of book equity. Equity CAGR is rejected as a growth anchor; the forward price+volume+backlog build is used instead.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC (no interest-income strip: net borrower). Owner-FCF CAGRs: FY2020 3,896 -> FY2022 5,584 -> FY2025 4,925. The negative 3yr owner-FCF CAGR is the capex supercycle, not deteriorating cash generation: OCF rose from 8,864 (FY2022) to 10,350 (FY2025) while capex rose from 3,173 to 5,261. SBC is only 0.5% of revenue and grew in line with revenue, so owner and reported FCF CAGRs are within 0.5pp of each other.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +7% (H1-2026 +8.8% incl. ~2% FX and ~1% acquisitions; Q3 guide carries no FX; adj. EPS guide $17.70-17.90 reaffirmed). FY2027-28 +5.5% as the $8.1B sale-of-gas backlog converts (Fort Saskatchewan, Beaumont, US electronics wins), then taper to 3% nominal (2% price + ~1% volume) by year 10.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: Pre-SBC EBITDA margin 37.8% FY2025 (incl. 0.8pp restructuring), 38.6% H1-2026. Base assumes ~20bp/yr of pricing-and-productivity expansion for four years to a 39% plateau; management flagged Americas margin slippage in Q2-2026, so expansion is slower than the 50-80bp/yr Linde delivered 2019-2024.
base.da_rationale: D&A 11.1% of revenue FY2025. Non-deductible merger amortisation (~$0.8B/yr) rolls off over the horizon while depreciation on the backlog build rises; net drift to 10.5%.
base.capex_rationale: FY2026 guided $5.5-6.0B (~16% of revenue) against the $8.1B backlog; as start-ups complete, project capex normalises toward a 12% maintenance-plus-growth level (FY2021-22 ran ~10% with little backlog; terminal 12% vs D&A 10.5% funds 3% growth).
base.cash_tax_rationale: 25.5% of engine EBIT ties to FY2025 taxes paid $2,274M / EBIT $8,923M (FY2024 25.7%). Drifts to 24% as non-deductible purchase-accounting amortisation (which depresses engine EBIT without reducing tax) rolls off; Pillar Two keeps the floor above the 22% GAAP rate.
base.narrative: Backlog converts on schedule, base business compounds at price + modest volume, margins plateau ~39% pre-SBC, capex normalises to 12% of revenue by year 7; terminal 20x owner FCF (the cap binds marginally: Gordon at 8%/3% is 20.6x).

bull.narrative: Electronics and clean-hydrogen/CCS backlog keeps growing beyond $8B, volumes run 3-4% on top of 2% pricing, productivity restores the pre-2025 margin cadence to 40.5% pre-SBC, and project capex normalises faster (11.5%) as start-ups outpace new awards; exit at 22x owner FCF.

bear.narrative: Global industrial recession in 2027-28 cuts merchant and packaged volumes (price alone carries growth at ~2-2.5%), Americas margin slippage becomes a trend as cost inflation outruns pricing, clean-hydrogen/CCS projects slip or lose policy support so backlog capex continues (13%) without matching revenue, Pillar Two lifts cash tax; exit at 16x owner FCF.

scenario_narratives.base: Linde's base case is the business management describes: ~2% annual price attainment plus 2-3% volume as the record $8.1B sale-of-gas backlog (57% clean energy, with the Fort Saskatchewan/Dow and Beaumont projects and new US electronics contracts) starts up through 2026-28, decelerating to 3% nominal growth by year 10. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin expands only ~120bp from FY2025's 37.8% to a 39% plateau because the Q2-2026 Americas slippage shows pricing is no longer fully outrunning cost inflation. Capex, the swing factor, falls from the guided ~16% of revenue to 12% by FY2032 as project spend normalises, lifting the owner-FCF margin from ~14.7% in FY2026 to ~19.7% at terminal. 8% WACC, 3% terminal growth, 20x terminal cap binding.
scenario_narratives.bull: The bull axes are backlog momentum and margin cadence: proposal activity in electronics and decarbonisation keeps the sale-of-gas backlog above $8B indefinitely, volumes run 3-4% rather than 2%, and productivity restores the 50-80bp/yr margin expansion of 2019-24 to a 40.5% pre-SBC plateau. Project capex normalises faster (11.5% of revenue) because start-ups outpace new awards. Terminal 3.5% growth and a 22x owner-FCF exit, consistent with the premium the market pays the Linde/Air Liquide duopoly.
scenario_narratives.bear: The bear axes are the industrial cycle, the margin trend and policy dependence of the backlog. A 2027-28 manufacturing recession removes volume growth (merchant and packaged correlate with PMI) while take-or-pay contracts hold revenue to the ~2% price line; Americas margin slippage continues as energy and labour inflation outruns price (37% pre-SBC plateau); clean-hydrogen/CCS projects slip or lose incentive support so capex stays at 13% of revenue without matching revenue conversion, and the $28B of debt funding buybacks and capex becomes a constraint on returns. Pillar Two lifts cash tax to 26.5%; exit at 16x owner FCF with 2.5% terminal growth. Not a solvency scenario: an A-rated balance sheet and $10B+ of operating cash flow survive it.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Shifted from the 15/50/35 house default to 20/50/30. Bear raised to 20% because total debt has risen from $15.9B (FY2023) to $28.0B (Q2-2026) while the capex supercycle must be executed, and the Q2-2026 margin slippage is a live data point rather than a hypothetical; it is not raised further because take-or-pay contracts, energy pass-through and an A rating make the bear a margin-and-growth case, not a solvency one. Bull trimmed to 30% because it needs three independent things to go right at once: sustained backlog replenishment, a return to the pre-2025 margin cadence, and faster capex normalisation.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Linde is valued as a stream of owner free cash flow: SBC (0.5% of revenue) fully expensed with the share count held flat, cash taxes at the rate actually paid rather than the GAAP provision, and the backlog capex supercycle modelled explicitly over 10 years rather than capitalising FY2025's depressed FCF or an adjusted-EPS multiple. The result is dominated by two choices, both disclosed: an 8% USD WACC and a 20x terminal owner-FCF cap. The market price embeds a materially lower discount rate for this duopoly compounder; the required-return table shows which rate today's price implies, and that gap is the finding rather than a modelling error.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal value share: with a 10-year horizon and a 20x cap, roughly two-thirds of enterprise value is terminal; the WACC x g grid and the required-return table bound this.
Capex normalisation is the single largest driver of the owner-FCF margin ramp; if project capex stays at 15-16% of revenue permanently the base value falls toward the bear case.
Margin: each 1pp of pre-SBC EBITDA margin at terminal is worth roughly $25-30/share.
Debt vintage: net debt $23.1B at 2026-06-30 already reflects H1-2026 distributions; the Q3-2026 balance sheet (due early November) will move it by the H2 buyback pace (~$0.8B/quarter).

Non-deductible merger amortisation makes the engine's EBIT-based cash tax rate higher than the GAAP ETR; the path drifts down as it rolls off, but if the roll-off is slower than assumed, taxes are modestly overstated (conservative).
Metrics.csv TotalDebt (25,626) is mis-constructed (double-counts the current portion, omits short-term borrowings); the DCF uses the filer's combined-debt tag (28,013).
